public_rationale: CNBC reported $13.1 billion of realized 2025 revenue, above the stated $12.7 billion benchmark. That contradicts the numerical reading that OpenAI was likely to miss the projection. It does not disprove the weaker possibility that reaching the target involved difficulty.
limitations: The verdict depends on interpreting ‘have trouble hitting’ as a likely shortfall.
The evidence is reputable news reporting based on unnamed sources, rather than public audited accounts.
The separate loss forecast is outside this normalized claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI will struggle to reach its $12.7 billion 2025 revenue projection.

statement.excerpt: To be clear, OpenAI, by my estimates, has only made around $5.26 billion this year (and will have trouble hitting its $12.7 billion revenue projection for 2025), and will likely lose more than $10 billion to do so.

our_interpretation: Assess the normalized revenue forecast only, excluding the separate year-to-date revenue and loss assertions in the same sentence.
The ordinary numerical reading is that OpenAI was likely to fall short of $12.7 billion in realized calendar-2025 revenue.
‘Have trouble’ could instead mean difficulty despite eventual success. Revenue attainment tests the numerical reading, not how difficult attainment felt.
Use estimate as the accounting basis because the passage discusses estimates and reported private-company projections, without specifying GAAP or another formal basis.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting places realized calendar-2025 revenue below $12.7 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reporting places realized calendar-2025 revenue at or above $12.7 billion.
